what: independent recompute by of3t-orchestrator of the row's fp32_softmax finding, from its own SMOFF and LADDER bundles
verified: the row's claim reproduces exactly: better at 5 of 7 blocks, 3 cross the median bar. Config fields confirm fp32_softmax False in every SMOFF bundle and True in every LADDER bundle.
headline: with fp32_softmax=False, FIVE of seven measured trunk blocks pass the 2.0e-02 median bar, against TWO with it on. This is the campaign's first lever that improves gradient parity.
block_32_is_explained: block 32 -- the 'magnitude right, direction wrong' block I flagged at pass 136 with median 0.09679, norm_ratio 1.0002 and cos 0.99563 -- improves 5.8x to 0.01679 and crosses the bar. fp32_softmax accounts for it.
and_it_does_nothing_for_40_and_47: blocks 40 and 47 read 1.004x and 1.009x -- unchanged. So the lever acts on blocks 0-32 and not on the end of the stack, which is independent evidence that block 47's per-track factor is a different mechanism.
what_it_does_NOT_settle: fp32_softmax=True was set for FORWARD accuracy. This arm is trunk backward only, one crop, one boundary, and says nothing about the forward argument that set it. It is a gradient-versus-forward tradeoff, not a free win.
it is RELEASE-GATED: flipping it changes shipped accuracy. The row reported it and did not flip it, and the default stays True. That is correct.
seven blocks of forty-eight, at crop 64 against one captured boundary.
what_it_licenses: a pre-registered A/B on the forward: if fp32_softmax=False costs nothing measurable on fold accuracy at shipped sizes, it becomes a candidate default change worth 3 of 7 blocks crossing the bar. If it costs forward accuracy, the campaign has found a real tension between forward and gradient parity and should say so -- that is a finding either way.
